intro: Screens, passwords, uploads and the words you need to talk about life online.
p.estar enganchado a.nota: Enganchado/a agrees with the person: está enganchada al móvil.
p.el celular: the mobile phone, cell phone (Latin America)
p.el celular.nota: Common in Latin America; el móvil is usual in Spain. The initial c is normally pronounced like s in most of Latin America.
p.el wifi.nota: Wifi is commonly used as a masculine noun: el wifi.
p.colgar.nota: In online contexts colgar means to post or upload; on a phone it can also mean to hang up.
b1.texto:
Many everyday verbs for using devices are regular in the present: **descargar**, **subir**, **enviar**, **reenviar**, **borrar**, **guardar**, **instalar**, **actualizar**, **iniciar sesión**. **Colgar** (**cuelgo**) has an *o → ue* stem change and means to post something online as well as to hang up.

Loanwords are adapted to Spanish spelling and pronunciation: **el/la wifi**, **el clic**, **chatear**, **un blog**.

In Spain people usually say **el móvil** and **el ordenador**; across Latin America **el celular** and **la computadora** (or **el computador**) are the usual terms.

To read an email address aloud: **@** is **arroba**, a dot is **punto**, **-** is **guion**, and **_** is **guion bajo**. So *ana.ruiz@correo.es* is read *ana punto ruiz arroba correo punto es*.

b2.f1: Here you are. You're hooked on your phone, aren't you?
b2.f2: It's just that I want to upload the photos to social media.
b2.f3: There's no signal here. Do you have the wifi password?
b2.f4: No. I'm going to download the bar's app.
b2.f5: Better switch off the screen and talk to me.
b4.o1: I've left my battery at home.
b4.o1.explicacion: Quedarse sin is to run out of.
b5.pregunta: How do you read @ in an email address?
b5.o0.refuerzo: The standard name of the sign.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The sign has its own name: arroba.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Spanish does not read it as at.
b6.pregunta: Complete: I'm going to download the app.
b8.pregunta: In Mexico, what do people usually call «el móvil»?
b8.o0.refuerzo: The usual word across Latin America.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That is a computer, in Spain.
b8.o2.refuerzo: That is a computer, in Latin America.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write your opinion on the use of mobile phones: advantages, dangers and your own habits.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Debate aloud: should mobile phones be banned in schools?
b4.o0.explicacion: Me he quedado sin batería means the battery has run out or gone flat.
